Covariance Coverage of Incomplete Data

Source: R/missing_coverage.R
missing_coverage.Rd

Reports, for every pair of items, the number and proportion of cases on which both were observed (the covariance coverage), with each item's own response rate on the diagonal. A covariance or a regression slope is informed most directly by the cases that observed both of its variables, so the coverage of a pair is a first, model-free look at how much data stand behind the parameters that involve it. Full information maximum likelihood (FIML) uses every case, and the other variables can carry information about a pair with low coverage, but a pair with no jointly observed case leaves its covariance with no direct information at all: its fraction of missing information is then one (Savalei & Rhemtulla, 2012, p. 488). fraction_missing_information gives that fraction for each parameter of a fitted model.

Usage

missing_coverage(data, items = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data.frame.

items

Optional character vector naming the columns of data to describe; NULL (the default) uses every column. Any column type is allowed, since only whether a value is NA matters.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with one row per pair of items, the item itself included, in the order of items (the pairs \((i, j)\) with \(i \le j\)), and the columns var_1, var_2, n_both (the cases that observed both; for var_1 == var_2, the cases that observed the item), and coverage (n_both as a proportion of the cases with at least one observed item). The attributes are matrix (the symmetric coverage matrix), N_used (the denominator), N_all_missing, and min_coverage.

Details

The denominator of every proportion is the number of cases with at least one observed item, the cases a FIML fit uses. That is the denominator of lavaan::lavInspect(fit, "coverage"), which the matrix attribute reproduces for a single group fit to the same items; cases with every item missing are counted in the N_all_missing attribute instead.

References

Savalei, V., & Rhemtulla, M. (2012). On obtaining estimates of the fraction of missing information from full information maximum likelihood. Structural Equation Modeling, 19(3), 477–494. doi:10.1080/10705511.2012.687669

See also

missing_patterns for the patterns behind the coverage; fraction_missing_information for what the missing values cost each parameter of a FIML fit.

Other missing data: cov_fiml(), df_barnard_rubin(), df_missing(), fraction_missing_information(), missing_patterns()

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

# The revised paper form board (t25) and the flags test (t26) were
# given only at Grant-White, so every pair involving either is covered
# by the 145 Grant-White pupils, 48 percent of the 301.
spatial <- c("t1_visual_perception", "t2_cubes", "t3_paper_form_board",
             "t4_lozenges", "t25_paper_form_board_r", "t26_flags")
cov_tbl <- missing_coverage(holzinger_swineford, items = spatial)
cov_tbl
#>  var_1                  var_2                  n_both coverage
#>  t1_visual_perception   t1_visual_perception   301    1.000   
#>  t1_visual_perception   t2_cubes               301    1.000   
#>  t1_visual_perception   t3_paper_form_board    301    1.000   
#>  t1_visual_perception   t4_lozenges            301    1.000   
#>  t1_visual_perception   t25_paper_form_board_r 145    0.482   
#>  t1_visual_perception   t26_flags              145    0.482   
#>  t2_cubes               t2_cubes               301    1.000   
#>  t2_cubes               t3_paper_form_board    301    1.000   
#>  t2_cubes               t4_lozenges            301    1.000   
#>  t2_cubes               t25_paper_form_board_r 145    0.482   
#>  t2_cubes               t26_flags              145    0.482   
#>  t3_paper_form_board    t3_paper_form_board    301    1.000   
#>  t3_paper_form_board    t4_lozenges            301    1.000   
#>  t3_paper_form_board    t25_paper_form_board_r 145    0.482   
#>  t3_paper_form_board    t26_flags              145    0.482   
#>  t4_lozenges            t4_lozenges            301    1.000   
#>  t4_lozenges            t25_paper_form_board_r 145    0.482   
#>  t4_lozenges            t26_flags              145    0.482   
#>  t25_paper_form_board_r t25_paper_form_board_r 145    0.482   
#>  t25_paper_form_board_r t26_flags              145    0.482   
#>  t26_flags              t26_flags              145    0.482   
round(attr(cov_tbl, "matrix"), 2)
#>                        t1_visual_perception t2_cubes t3_paper_form_board
#> t1_visual_perception                   1.00     1.00                1.00
#> t2_cubes                               1.00     1.00                1.00
#> t3_paper_form_board                    1.00     1.00                1.00
#> t4_lozenges                            1.00     1.00                1.00
#> t25_paper_form_board_r                 0.48     0.48                0.48
#> t26_flags                              0.48     0.48                0.48
#>                        t4_lozenges t25_paper_form_board_r t26_flags
#> t1_visual_perception          1.00                   0.48      0.48
#> t2_cubes                      1.00                   0.48      0.48
#> t3_paper_form_board           1.00                   0.48      0.48
#> t4_lozenges                   1.00                   0.48      0.48
#> t25_paper_form_board_r        0.48                   0.48      0.48
